main_statement.paraphrase: There is a countable metric space in which distinct points are at distance at least 1, whose real Lipschitz-free space has the approximation property but no bounded approximation property. This answers Kalton's question negatively.

constructive_core.paraphrase: Thm blocks: for each p there is a bounded, 1-separated, countably infinite block M_p (diam <= 300p^2+150p+5) and a finite anchor set A_p such that every finite-rank operator of norm <= p moves some anchor evaluation by at least 1/2.

headline_corollaries.paraphrase: Equivalent norms on real ell_1 with 2B_p-BAP but not p-BAP; for p=1, not MAP (formalized).
F(M) is a separable Banach space that is not approximable, answering Kalton's Problem 1 negatively (NOT formalized).

flags.full_only_with_prior_results_detail: The headline needs no cited theorem: Prop coefficients is re-proved and AP of the wedge is proved directly (Kalton04 Prop 4.4 mentioned as an alternative). The Lean proves it from Mathlib alone.
flags.adds_corollaries_detail: (1) Cor renorming: real ell_1 has an equivalent norm failing MAP, answering negatively whether every equivalent norm on ell_1 has MAP (a classical open question; Kalton12 p.1260); formalized. (2) F(M) is a separable Banach space that is not approximable, answering Kalton's Problem 1 (Kalton12 p.1260) negatively; NOT formalized and depends on Kalton's net theorem.

B.note: Kalton's question (Kalton04 p.185; Godefroy-Ozawa Q1; Godefroy survey Problem 6.2) asked whether uniformly discrete free spaces always have BAP; the paper refutes it. A web check (Oct 2026) found the question listed as open before this release; Smith26 (countable complete discrete, non-uniformly-discrete, non-constructive via Bossard) is the closest prior result.

proof_architecture.claim: Reduction: Prop coefficients (bounded 1-separated => F ~ ell_1, 2B-BAP). The metric wedge of blocks M_p, with contractive inclusion/retractions, inherits each block's obstruction (so no lambda-BAP) and has AP via finite-block projections R_N. Cor renorming transports F(M_p) to ell_1. The nonlinear corollary follows from Kalton's net theorem.

Block construction: fix parameters; take a deterministic sequence of Delta-regular k-coloured multigraphs with iid-coloured-tree local statistics (paper: permutation model; Lean: large-girth Cayley quotients x all colourings). Label vertices by capped distances to colour classes; attach each vertex to the anchor of its label at distance R; join anchors by 2R + label distance. Get separation 1, diam <= B_p, 1-Lipschitz labels, small balls inside one graph, <= H uncapped coordinates.

From operator to measures: a finite-rank T_0 with ||T_0||<=p and anchor error < 1/2 is perturbed to T with finite support S, ||T||<=2p, anchor error < 1. Affine signed measures mu_x on S have TV <= V and int b_x d mu_x >= 3L/4 (anchor at distance R, bump slope L/K).

Rare matched walks: with S fixed, compatibility forces colours into sets of size <= H, transitions have <= Q successors, so the fraction of roots starting a matched walk of length n is <= |S|(H/k)(Delta Q H/k)^n + o(1); pick n then a large graph with bad fraction < 1/(20V).
Records: at good vertices define continuation records r_x(e,j) and exceptional incidences (strict argmax). Any compatible close pair across an edge has j in E_e or j' in E_{e-bar}.

Edge tests: f_e = b_x on S\E_e, -b_y on S\E_{e-bar}, extended by McShane and clipped. Pairing with mu_x - mu_y is >= 3L/2 - 2L(discarded variation) and <= 2p. Averaging over oriented incidences: discarded variation averages < 1/10 (one exceptional direction per state, degree > 20V; bad vertices rare). Contradiction 2p > 11p.
Assemble: Thm blocks for every p; then Thm main and Cor renorming (formalized), plus the unformalized nonlinear corollary.

eureka_candidates.item: I32 (+I30, I33): opposing edge tests with exceptional discard sets and incidence averaging
for: Not a subterm of the goal or of L: the goal speaks of finite-rank operators and anchors; the proof manufactures, for every oriented edge, a 1-Lipschitz functional that is +bump(x) and -bump(y) on the operator's support minus a combinatorially chosen discard set.
It is where the finite-dimensionality of the range (finite S) is actually exploited against the infinite locally-tree-like structure; every other step is preparation.

No near-equivalent found in a quick search of Lipschitz-extension / free-space literature (Naor almost-extension, Naor-Rabani extension from finite subsets, Godefroy-Ozawa, Brudnyi-Brudnyi): those bound extension or projection constants, not arbitrary finite-rank operators via edge-by-edge opposing tests.
Lean confirms it is load-bearing: edge_test -> finite_support_impossible -> obstruction (dominated share 0.37-0.39 for the latter two).
against: The discard rule is an adaptation of a named precedent (Ben-David et al. 2024, continuation-length parent selection), so its hardest sub-step is transfer.

Once one decides to compare neighbouring measures by opposing bumps, the conflict on close cross pairs is forced, and discarding a sparse set of (state, direction) pairs is a natural repair; a judge may call the whole complex N2.
Averaging over edges against a degree-diluted error is a standard expander/Poincare pattern.

route_differences_lean_vs_paper: Graph family: the paper uses random permutation-model multigraphs with iid colours and a local-limit lemma, then fixes a deterministic realization sequence. Lean uses Cayley graphs of finite permutation quotients of the free group on 20V+2 generators acting on word balls (girth > N), crossed with ALL colourings, so the bad-root bound is an exact count (ColorCounting.cardinal_identity) and the walk length n equals the component index N. No probability appears anywhere in Lean.
Degree and colours: Lean takes degree = 2(20V+2) > 20V and colors = 2*degree*Q*H + 1, concrete instances of the paper's 'choose Delta with V/Delta<1/20' and 'k > 2 Delta Q H'.

Metric: Lean uses a complete weighted graph with fallback weight 4R+cap on non-edges and its integer path closure; diameter <= 4R+D is then immediate. The paper uses the sparse weighted graph and bounds routes through anchors.
Finite-support reduction: Lean composes T_0 with a finite coordinate truncation (exploiting the ell_1 structure of the bounded block); the paper perturbs a basis of the range.
AP of the wedge: Lean collapses onto a retained finite union of blocks, which is itself bounded and separated, and applies its 2B-BAP; the paper sums per-block operators I_p T_p P_p.
Labels: Lean defines capped colour distances by Nat.find over walks in the port graph (PortGraph.label), equivalent to the paper's graph distances.
Dead code: BlockPaths.lean (SourcePath, source_shortest_path) is not on the proof DAG according to the extractor.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found. The obstruction (sections 4-6) was checked line by line, and both comparator targets are formalized in Lean with no sorry/axiom and comparator-faithful statements. The one unformalized major claim is the nonlinear corollary (Kalton's Problem 1).
checked: Lemma finite-support: eta < min{p, 1/(2B)} gives ||T|| < 2p and anchor error < 1/2 + eta B < 1.
Lemma measure-bounds: sign test has Lip <= 2 by 1-separation, so TV <= 2||T delta_x|| + 1 <= 1+4pB; bump mass L - (L/K)(2pR+1) >= 3L/4.
Lemma rare-walks: matched => colour of x_s in C_{j_s}; at most Delta^n nonbacktracking walks with distinct vertices on the tree, |S|Q^n state sequences, probability (H/k)^{n+1}.
Lemma exceptional-directions: A_x >= r_x(e,j) >= 1+A_y >= 1+r_y(e-bar,j') >= 2+A_x when neither is exceptional. The extended walk has length < n automatically because x is good.
Lemma edge-test: positive b_x(j) with d(j,j') < 2L forces both compatibilities (label triangle inequality < 1+K+2L), hence a discard; consistency on P∩Q via j=j'.
Final count: E|mu|(E_e) <= V/Delta + V beta < 1/10; 3L/2 - 4L/10 = 11p > 2p.
Wedge: triangle inequality case analysis; retractions 1-Lipschitz; R_N contractive projection; AP via R_N then block BAPs.
Lean: all of the above except Lemma local-limit (replaced by a deterministic construction) and the nonlinear corollary.
residual_concerns: The nonlinear corollary (F(M) not approximable, answering Kalton's Problem 1) relies on the exact form of Kalton12 Thm 4.4 (a uniform Lipschitz bound for finite-range net maps approximating finite sets). It is not formalized and was not checked against Kalton's text. A literature source notes that a counterexample to Kalton's Problem 1 would give an ell_1 renorming without MAP; consistent with the paper, which proves the latter directly (formalized).

Three long-standing questions are claimed at once (Kalton's BAP question, MAP for equivalent norms on ell_1, Kalton's approximability problem). The first two are machine-checked modulo comparator definitions; the claims are extraordinary and unreviewed.

Comparator fidelity: FreeSpace is the closure of span of evaluations in the dual of Lip0 with the slope norm; HasAP/HasBAP use '∃ η < ε, errors <= η'. Both agree with the paper. BlockStatement asks only Countable (not infinite), harmless as argued.
The paper's Lemma local-limit is a standard but un-formalized probabilistic argument; Lean's independent deterministic route removes any dependence on it for the formal result.
No reasoning trace for this family; provenance of the record idea (TCS paper) is explicit in the text.
